title: A longer piece, learned in sections
summary: Split a longer piece into sections and spread learning them across the week's sittings with a schedule.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil
a sheet of paper for the practice schedule

figure.alt: Four boxes stacked, one for each section a longer piece is split into, learned one section per sitting on a written schedule, spread across the week.

steps.title: A longer piece, learned in sections
steps.body:
A longer piece feels impossible when it is one unbroken wall of notes. Cut into sections it is just several short pieces, learned one at a time, the same as anything else you have practised.

1. Play through the whole piece slowly, and split it into three or four sections by ear, the way you have mapped pieces before.
2. Write a short schedule: which section each sitting this week will learn.
3. Learn only that sitting's section, hard bars first, and do not rush ahead to the next one.
4. From the second sitting on, play back every section already learned before starting the new one.

The schedule matters as much as the practice. Without one, the easy first section gets played every day and the last section never gets its fair share of attention.

figure.alt: The same four boxes, one section learned or reviewed each sitting, so the last section still gets its fair share of practice by the end of the week.

steps.title: Four sittings
steps.body: Fifteen minutes each. Tick a sitting when it is done. Days do not matter; sittings do.
checklist: Sitting 1: split the piece into sections, write the schedule, learn section one
Sitting 2: review section one, then learn section two
Sitting 3: review sections one and two, then learn section three
Sitting 4: play every section learned so far in order, then once as if recording
An old piece played once, noticing its own sections

steps.title: Record this week's version
steps.prompt: Say the name of the piece, then play every section learned so far, in order, hands in the frame.
